Spatial-temporal convolutions address local spatio-spectral regularities, while LSTMs handle sequential dependencies across time. However, naive fusion of these operators leads to catastrophic forgetting and over-parameterization. Regularization stabilizes training but may introduce bias if hyper-parameters are mis-tuned. The resulting composite models must balance expressiveness against computational efficiency for real-time deployment. Failure occurs when priors on stationarity are violated, causing divergence in predictive distributions. Cross-layer veto conditions enforce mutual exclusivity among competing hypotheses to prevent redundancy. Anti-collinearity penalties ensure that each primitive contributes orthogonal information, improving interpretability and robustness.
